title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Harrowing Story of the North Hollywood Shootout
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the February 28, 1997 North Hollywood shootout, a bank robbery in North Hollywood, Los Angeles, carried out by Larry Eugene Phillips Jr. and Emil Mattiseranu (the "High Incident Bandits"). The pair were heavily armed with assault rifles, body armor and steel-cased ammunition, and had earlier robbed Brinks and Bank of America targets. The episode covers their backgrounds, the 1993 traffic stop where they were caught with a bank robbery kit and got a light sentence, the robbery itself, the roughly 44-minute firefight with LAPD and other agencies, the deaths of both robbers, the lasting push toward police militarization (the 1997 Defense Authorization section 1033 surplus transfers), and PTSD counseling for officers. The episode also includes a listener follow-up from Michelle Grua correcting details about Kenton Grua from a previous episode on his Grand Canyon river adventure. This episode is part of a fall true crime playlist.

segments.title: Cold open teaser
segments.summary: Josh introduces the North Hollywood robbery as a link to the militarization of police episode.

segments.title: Opening banter on heists
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter about whether the event counts as a heist and how surreal it was.

segments.title: Background of the robbers
segments.summary: Larry Phillips Jr. and Emil Mattiseranu are introduced. Phillips controlled Mattiseranu, both met as bodybuilders at Gold's Gym in 1989, and Phillips' early crimes and movie inspirations are described. Phillips' criminal father and his childhood are covered, along with Mattiseranu's immigration and his mother Valerie Nicolescu's care home business.

segments.title: Family care home and Nicolescu's allegations
segments.summary: The family ran a residential care home for disabled residents that faced mistreatment allegations and fire code closure. After the shootout, police found a disabled woman locked in a Pasadena building, and Nicolescu was sentenced for neglect and later for social security fraud in 2002.

segments.title: Guns, steel-cased ammunition and smuggling
segments.summary: The men shared a love of assault rifles. Phillips allegedly imported thousands of rounds of illegal steel-cased ammunition from Russia, as described in a National Geographic documentary.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Sponsor break.

segments.title: 1993 Glendale arrest and the earlier robberies
segments.summary: In 1993 police found a bank robbery kit in their rental car and the pair pled to a misdemeanor, serving about four months, and got their weapons back. They went on to commit the High Incident Bandits robberies: a 1995 Brinks armored truck robbery in which a driver was killed, and 1996 robberies of two Bank of America branches netting about 1.3 to 1.7 million dollars.

segments.title: Bank robbery economics and high living
segments.summary: Hosts discuss how rare large bank hauls were compared with typical bank robbery takes, and how the men spent the money on cars and watches.

segments.title: North Hollywood location and Barry tangent
segments.summary: The robbery target was a Bank of America on Laurel Canyon Boulevard in North Hollywood. Hosts make a tangent about the HBO show Barry.

segments.title: The February 28, 1997 bank robbery
segments.summary: On a Friday at the end of the month, the two men entered the Bank of America in body armor and masks, firing into the air. Police watched them walk in. They had taken phenobarbital to calm their nerves and were timing the robbery with stopwatches.

segments.title: Inside the bank and the hostage vault
segments.summary: Bank staff were locked in a vault. One woman texted police from her cell phone, and an officer misread LOL. The robbers shot a safe, ruining money, and took about 300,000 dollars.

segments.title: Exit and the surrounding police
segments.summary: The robbers walked out to find more than 300 officers from five agencies and police helicopters. Dye packs had ruined much of the cash.

segments.title: Firefight begins and LAPD outgunned
segments.summary: The robbers fired at everything that moved. Police patrol officers were outgunned, bullets went through their car doors and concrete, and their handguns could not penetrate body armor. Officers went to a gun store to rearm, and SWAT arrived after about 18 minutes.

segments.title: Kill zone, injuries and dentist rescue
segments.summary: Two bystanders were shot, several officers were injured, and officers were pinned down in the kill zone. Dentist Jorge Montes treated injured officers in his office across the street and left shrapnel in one officer's ankle.

segments.title: Split-up, Phillips' death and Mattiseranu's escape
segments.summary: The robbers got into a white Chevy Celebrity and then split up; Phillips walked down a side street and was shot eleven times. He was shot in the hand, then either shot himself or was hit fatally by police.

segments.title: Archwood Street pursuit and final capture
segments.summary: Mattiseranu drove on residential Archwood Street where the street was not closed, carjacked a jeep pickup, and was shot 28 times by SWAT officers from under the car, then surrendered.

segments.title: Casualties and the EMT controversy
segments.summary: Twelve officers and eight bystanders were injured, all survived; the two robbers died. Mattiseranu asked for death and bled out while officers kept EMTs away. A lawsuit ended in a mistrial and no further case.

segments.title: Aftermath: police militarization and PTSD counseling
segments.summary: The 1997 defense spending act section 1033 allowed surplus military weapons to go to police, which fed police militarization. PTSD counseling for officers also became more common afterward. Mentions of Grand Theft Auto V and the film Forty-Four Minutes.

segments.title: Listener mail intro
segments.summary: Chuck introduces a listener follow-up.

segments.title: Michelle Grua correction on Kenton Grua episode
segments.summary: Michelle Grua corrects details from the earlier Kenton Grua Grand Canyon episode, including his moccasins, booze resupply, fine amount, a second oar lock idea, and his cause of death, which she says was spontaneous coronary artery dissection rather than a collision. Hosts apologize.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh thanks Michelle Grua and Chuck, and gives the email address for feedback. The episode closes with the iHeart outro.
